s: a stitch in time saves nine
m: Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one later.
e: He patched the leak at once, because a stitch in time saves nine.

s: better late than never
m: It is better to do something late than not to do it at all.
e: She apologised a week after the party; better late than never.

s: time and tide wait for no man
m: Time does not stop for anyone, so do not delay.
e: Book the tickets now, because time and tide wait for no man.

s: all things come to those who wait
m: Patience is often rewarded.
e: The job offer took months, but all things come to those who wait.

s: rome was not built in a day
m: Big things take a long time and many steps.
e: Be patient with your business; Rome was not built in a day.

s: strike while the iron is hot
m: Act at the best moment, while the chance is there.
e: The shop is full today, so strike while the iron is hot and ask for the order.

s: the early bird catches the worm
m: People who start early get the advantage.
e: We queued at six, because the early bird catches the worm.

s: practice makes perfect
m: Doing something again and again makes you good at it.
e: Keep playing the scale; practice makes perfect.

s: where there is a will there is a way
m: If you really want to do something, you will find a way.
e: She studied at night after work, because where there is a will there is a way.

s: many hands make light work
m: A job is easier when many people share it.
e: Everyone helped to clean the hall, and many hands make light work.

s: actions speak louder than words
m: What people do matters more than what they say.
e: He promised often, but actions speak louder than words.

s: slow and steady wins the race
m: Steady, careful work beats quick, uneven effort.
e: Study a little each day; slow and steady wins the race.

s: a bad workman always blames his tools
m: A person who does poor work makes excuses about the equipment.
e: Do not blame the pen; a bad workman always blames his tools.

s: well begun is half done
m: A good start makes the rest of the job easier.
e: Write the outline first; well begun is half done.

s: a penny saved is a penny earned
m: Saving money is as good as earning it.
e: He took a packed lunch, because a penny saved is a penny earned.

s: do not put all your eggs in one basket
m: Do not risk everything on one plan or one thing.
e: Spread your savings; do not put all your eggs in one basket.

s: money does not grow on trees
m: Money is limited and has to be earned.
e: We cannot buy everything, because money does not grow on trees.

s: a fool and his money are soon parted
m: People who are careless spend their money quickly.
e: He lost his bonus in a week; a fool and his money are soon parted.

s: you cannot take it with you
m: Money and things stay behind when you die, so enjoy and share them.
e: They gave generously, because you cannot take it with you.

s: a friend in need is a friend indeed
m: A true friend helps you when you are in trouble.
e: He drove all night to help me; a friend in need is a friend indeed.

s: birds of a feather flock together
m: People with similar tastes and habits keep company.
e: The two cricket fans became friends; birds of a feather flock together.

s: a man is known by the company he keeps
m: You can judge a person by the friends they choose.
e: Choose your friends well, because a man is known by the company he keeps.

s: too many cooks spoil the broth
m: Too many people on one job make a mess of it.
e: Let one person plan the trip; too many cooks spoil the broth.

s: two heads are better than one
m: Two people thinking together solve problems better than one.
e: Let us decide together; two heads are better than one.

s: good fences make good neighbours
m: Clear limits between people keep the peace.
e: We agreed where the wall stands, because good fences make good neighbours.

s: look before you leap
m: Think about the risks before you act.
e: Read the contract first; look before you leap.

s: do not judge a book by its cover
m: Do not decide about someone or something by its looks alone.
e: The shop looks plain, but do not judge a book by its cover.

s: curiosity killed the cat
m: Asking too many questions or poking around can bring trouble.
e: Leave the locked drawer alone; curiosity killed the cat.

s: every cloud has a silver lining
m: There is something good even in a bad situation.
e: Losing the job pushed her to start a business; every cloud has a silver lining.

s: it is no use crying over spilt milk
m: Do not waste time upset about something that cannot be undone.
e: The glass is broken, but it is no use crying over spilt milk.

s: the pen is mightier than the sword
m: Writing and ideas have more lasting power than force.
e: The campaign won by argument; the pen is mightier than the sword.

s: knowledge is power
m: Knowing things gives you strength and choices.
e: Read the rules before you sign; knowledge is power.

s: honesty is the best policy
m: It is wiser and better to tell the truth.
e: Admit the mistake now; honesty is the best policy.

s: pride comes before a fall
m: Too much pride leads to failure.
e: He bragged before the match and lost; pride comes before a fall.

s: people who live in glass houses should not throw stones
m: Do not criticise others for faults you have yourself.
e: You are late too, so people who live in glass houses should not throw stones.

s: a leopard cannot change its spots
m: People do not change their basic nature.
e: He will not stop boasting; a leopard cannot change its spots.

s: a rolling stone gathers no moss
m: A person who keeps moving does not settle or build things up.
e: He changed jobs every year; a rolling stone gathers no moss.

s: nothing ventured, nothing gained
m: If you do not take a risk, you cannot win.
e: Apply for the job; nothing ventured, nothing gained.

s: better safe than sorry
m: It is wiser to be careful than to regret it later.
e: Take an umbrella; better safe than sorry.

s: do not count your chickens before they hatch
m: Do not rely on a good result before it has happened.
e: You have not signed yet, so do not count your chickens before they hatch.

s: fortune favours the bold
m: People who take brave action are often rewarded.
e: She asked for the top job and got it; fortune favours the bold.

s: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
m: A sure small thing is better than a big uncertain one.
e: Take the offer now; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

s: do not bite off more than you can chew
m: Do not accept more work than you can handle.
e: Finish one project first; do not bite off more than you can chew.

s: every dog has its day
m: Everyone gets a good moment sooner or later.
e: The quiet player scored the winner; every dog has its day.

s: what goes around comes around
m: How you treat others comes back to you.
e: He was unkind to staff and later lost his own job; what goes around comes around.

s: the grass is always greener on the other side
m: Other people's situations always look better than your own.
e: She wants his job, he wants hers; the grass is always greener on the other side.

s: there is no place like home
m: Home is the most comfortable place of all.
e: After the long trip, there is no place like home.

s: all is well that ends well
m: If the result is good, earlier problems do not matter.
e: The trip had trouble, but all is well that ends well.

s: when the cat is away, the mice will play
m: People enjoy more freedom when the person in charge is absent.
e: The class got noisy when the teacher left; when the cat is away the mice will play.
